questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country and particularly liked Melbourne when i travelled around Australia some years ago. Good university with interesting subjects also important

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Incredibly happy with everything, genuinely had such a good time while i also achieved my academic goals

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly unproblematic, good orientation program organised by the university for all exchange students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The orientation program provided all the information i needed, no further assistance required

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got very lucky, as i have a friend in Australia whose friend was looking for a housemate. Ended up living with  Australians who were wonderful and became close friends. Before i got the room they were also advertising it on the facebook-group Fairy Floss Real Estate, which is a good place to look for renting or subletting

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Rent prices are fairly similar to Denmark, with variation of course, so you can end up paying more or less than you are used to. Cost of living is quite high, and groceries and such can be surprisingly expensive. Not too bad compared to Denmark though, so nothing shocking.

Most important thing. It gets cold. Seriously. Australian houses appear to be insulated with cardboard and most of them don't have heating. As a result, indoor temperatures get very low. To put some numbers on it, for the first month i was here my room was usually 12°C, occasionally getting above 14. Even approaching summer, my room was rarely more than 18 degrees. Wearing shoes and jackets indoors is perfectly normal, so seriously, bring warm clothing!
Of course there is big variation from house to house, so some will be warmer, but be prepared for this

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 5 if this means how happy was i with the house i ended up with, i absolutely loved it. If it means university student housing then i wouldn't know

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All happened online in the student portal. Straightforward and simple to figure out. Changing subjects close to the beginning of semester start was completely unproblematic

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 is the student service that can help with all questions related to university admin. They are very helpful, but can be a bit difficult to get an appointment with as they are very busy, especially around registration period

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely, was accepting into all of them

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive having chosen some subjects from home, but don't be too bothered about whether you have chosen the right ones. You have plenty of time to change your mind once you arrive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally very good and interesting. One slight issue is that Australian students have to do a certain amount of breadth subjects as part of their course. This means subjects in fields different from what you normally study. As a result, most subjects have to start out at an introductory level, to teach the breadth students the basics. This means that the academic level can seem a bit low at first

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did three second year courses and one first year course. In hindsight probably could have gone for more advanced courses, but they were all interesting, and covered topics i hadn't been taught back home

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More centered around lectures, with everything needed for the exams covered in lectures. There was not much need for further independent reading. Practical classes where the knowledge from lectures was applied was somewhat reminiscent of the style of teaching in the Danish gymnasie.
The whole grading structure is different to UCPH. Each subject has its own marking structure, but typically you get marks throughout the course that all count towards your final grade. For example in one of my subjects there was a weekly quiz, the results of which counted for 20% of the final grade. Exams usually only count for about 50% of the grade, with the rest being based on assignments, presentations or quizzes done throughout the semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Wonders of the Weather
Dangerous Earth
Economic Tools for the Environment
Past Climates: Icehouse to Greenhouse

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic Tools for the Environment was very enjoyable and interesting as well. It is based around valuing nature and biodiversity and coming up with economic cases and methods to protect them. The style of teaching is quite independent and students are encouraged to take an active interest and role in the subject.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing unexpected as such

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport is a tricky one to define. Trams are the primary way of getting around the city, and every trip costs 4,60 dollars (20-25 kroner) no matter if it takes 2 minutes or 2 hours. This means the value for money changes dramatically depending on how far you have to travel. However, at no point during my stay here did i meet a ticket inspector on a tram. Make of that what you will

In terms of travelling around the country, domestic plane tickets were surprisingly expensive but nothing that breaks the budget if you have set aside money specifically for this.

Beer is insanely expensive, roughly twice the price you pay in Denmark. At bars and such, prices are pretty similar though. Eating out is a bit cheaper in Melbourne, with lots of good food available for decent prices.

And for some reason peppers are insanely expensive, but this is admittedly a minor issue

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Huge amounts of clubs and societies to choose from. Also pretty much every sport you can think of is available through university

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Plenty. Especially the Melbourne University Exchange Society (MUSEX) organise lots of fun events.
Lots of clubs, societies and sports, which are all introduced during the orientation period

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining a sports team is a good way of meeting people, doesn't have to be at a serious level. For example, netball is surprisingly good fun, and fairly easy to pick up

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend getting into Australian Rules Football. AFL, commonly known as footy, is very entertaining and going to games at the MCG (Melbourne Cricket Ground, huge stadium) is a great experience. More importantly, it is a really good conversation topic. Absolutely everyone in Melbourne follows it and supports a team, so picking a team and knowing just the basics is very useful when getting to know locals

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Australians are incredibly open and friendly, and brilliant at making people feel welcome straight away

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
As mentioned, footy is a great way to break the ice and start a conversation, works with almost everybody in Melbourne. Again, Australians are typically open to new people in a way we are not used to in Denmark, so approaching people in social settings is a lot easier
And then living with Australians certainly helped for me as well

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Acknowledgement of Aboriginal Peoples as the traditional owners of the land of Australia is very important in society. Australians are very aware that terrible atrocities were committed against indigenous people in relatively recent history, and reconciliation is a constantly ongoing process. At first, as an outsider, the constant acknowledgements of country can seem as superficial political correctness, but it really is very important to most Australians and respected by everyone. Engaging and educating yourself on the topic is a good way of feeling more connected and part of the local culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Australian openness and friendliness, it is great when you are adapting to a new place on the other side of the world, and helps making friends

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the orientation period to get everything sorted for the start of semester. Because of the running grading system, it is good to be on it from week 1
Don't postpone starting things such as joining clubs or sports teams. Time goes by quickly, and the earlier you start, the more you will get out of it
Campus is big and very nice, with lots of good spots to study. It is an enjoyable place to spend time, so make sure to explore it and find the nice spots. Lots of hidden gems around

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get an Australian bank account as soon as possible. It makes things so much easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The friendships i have made (cliche, sorry), especially with my housemates and their extended group of friends.
Testing myself academically in another system and learning from a different perspective was great as well

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going back to Denmark. I really feel at home in Melbourne, and readjusting to life back in Copenhagen will be difficult

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go for it! It's good fun

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
